title: Fully powered mixed-ratio conjecture for arithmetic functions
statement:
Let $\varphi(n)$, $\psi(n)$ and $\sigma(n)$ denote the Euler totient, Dedekind psi and sum-of-divisors functions, respectively. For integers $k\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, form the three quantities $\varphi^k(n)(\psi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))$, $\psi^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))$ and $\sigma^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\psi^k(n))$. **Fully powered mixed-ratio conjecture.** For every integers $k\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, we have

$$
\frac{\varphi^k(n)(\psi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))}{\psi^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))+\sigma^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\psi^k(n))}+\frac{\psi^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))}{\varphi^k(n)(\psi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))+\sigma^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\psi^k(n))}+\frac{\sigma^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\psi^k(n))}{\varphi^k(n)(\psi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))+\psi^k(n)(\varphi^k(n)+\sigma^k(n))}\geq\frac{5(n-1)^{2k}+5(n^2-1)^k+2(n+1)^{2k}}{\big(3(n-1)^k+(n+1)^k\big)\big((n-1)^k+(n+1)^k\big)}.
$$

This proposed inequality is not resolved in the supplied text.

progress.tldr: A reader-written complete-proof attempt appeared, but no independent source has checked it, so the conjecture is not established.
progress.summary:
S. I. Dimitrov’s June 2026 preprint records the inequality as Conjecture 9 for all $k \geq 1$ and $n \geq 2$. The preprint supplies no proof or counterexample.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12484)*

**Posted attempt**

A reader-written argument claims a complete proof: after setting $x=\varphi(n)^k$, $y=\psi(n)^k$, $z=\sigma(n)^k$, it asserts $0<x\leq(n-1)^k<(n+1)^k\leq y\leq z$, proves monotonicity of the resulting expression, and obtains the conjectured bound. The attempt has not been independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture is recorded in a June 2026 preprint, while a complete proof has been posted in discussion but remains unverified; no verified proof or counterexample is known.

*Caveats. The proof claim appears only in reader-written discussion and has no independent mathematical verification.*

solutions.body:
**Complete proof for every \(n\ge2\) and \(k\ge1\).**

Set
\[
x=\varphi(n)^k,\quad y=\psi(n)^k,\quad z=\sigma(n)^k,\quad
a=(n-1)^k,\quad b=(n+1)^k.
\]
The Euler-product formulas imply \(0<x\le a<b\le y\le z\): indeed,
\(\varphi(n)\le n-1\), \(\psi(n)\ge n+1\), and
\(\sigma(p^e)\ge p^e+p^{e-1}=\psi(p^e)\).

Put
\[
A=x(y+z),\quad B=y(x+z),\quad C=z(x+y),\qquad
G=\frac A{B+C}+\frac B{A+C}+\frac C{A+B}.
\]
By homogeneity let \(r=x/y\) and \(t=z/y\), so \(0<r\le a/b<1\), \(t\ge1\).
A direct common-denominator computation gives
\[
G(r,t)-G(r,1)
=\frac{r(t-1)P(r,t-1)}
{(r+1)(3r+1)(rt+r+2t)(rt+2r+t)(2rt+r+t)},
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(r,v)={}&(2r^4+4r^3+7r^2+8r+3)v^2\\
&+(4r^4-5r^3+8r^2+19r+6)v\\
&+(1-r)(3r+1)(5r+3).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every denominator factor is positive. All coefficients of \(P\) are nonnegative for \(0<r\le1\), since its linear coefficient equals
\[
4r^4+5r^2(1-r)+3r^2+19r+6>0.
\]
Thus \(G(r,t)\ge G(r,1)\). Moreover,
\[
G(r,1)=\frac r{r+1}+\frac{2(r+1)}{3r+1},\qquad
\frac{d}{dr}G(r,1)
=\frac{(r-1)(5r+3)}{(r+1)^2(3r+1)^2}\le0.
\]
Since \(r\le a/b\),
\[
G\ge G(a/b,1)
=\frac{5a^2+5ab+2b^2}{(3a+b)(a+b)}
=
\frac{5(n-1)^{2k}+5(n^2-1)^k+2(n+1)^{2k}}
{\big(3(n-1)^k+(n+1)^k\big)\big((n-1)^k+(n+1)^k\big)}.
\]
This is the stated conjecture in full generality. Equality holds exactly when \(n\) is prime.
